doc.title: Chubby Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998

chapter: Woody Herman and the poll years
title: The Esquire winners and A Great Day in Harlem
summary: Chubby links the Esquire winners to the Great Day in Harlem photo organised by Jean Bach, and the reunion two years ago.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: No. I had forgotten all about that. But you know something so wild about this, Monk? This whole thing was responsible and was the birth of what is now known as “The Great Day in Harlem.”

Yeah. Because all these guys were in that photo. And that wasn’t called “Great Day in Harlem.” And a lady by the name of Jean Bach put this whole thing together, a lovely lady, too, and whoever was available — I mean Woody was not there because he was out of town, Lionel wasn’t there, Duke wasn’t there. But if you see that picture, I have a little picture of that with me—

Oh you have it? At any rate, it all of a sudden became “A Great Day in Harlem.” And then, this is wild, two years ago, they sent for Margo and I to go to New York City, to meet on the very stoop in Harlem that the original picture was taken in. There was only, well, ten of us there. And the rest of them were all gone, and it was a very wild get together. The next day, at the Silver Cup Studios in New York, they much have had a hundred thirty or so, around that area, of all the greatest musicians in the world showed up, to take more pictures.
